native_result.query: How is the advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students related to Socioeconomic status levels?
native_result.HypoA: The advantage in BA degree completion rates for Black students is more pronounced at lower SES levels with the interaction term for Socioeconomic status and being black having a coefficient of 0.7606
native_result.HypoB: With education right-censored at 1979, as-of-1979 BA completion (highest grade >=16) is too rare (32/8,870) to show any Black advantage at any SES level: Black vs non-Black/non-Hispanic rates are 0.10% vs 0.12% (Low SES), 0.65% vs 0.25% (Mid), 0.29% vs 0.63% (High), and race x SES-tertile interactions are non-significant (p = 0.42/0.71; MI-pooled p = 0.40/0.74). Family-of-origin SES strongly raises attainment at a similar rate for both groups (High-vs-Low log-odds +1.66 for BA, +1.03 for any postsecondary, both significant). The only supported Black advantage appears in the secondary outcome (any postsecondary, >=13): conditional on age and ASVAB achievement, Black respondents show higher postsecondary exposure (+1.08 log-odds, p<0.001), an advantage largest at Low/Mid SES and significantly attenuated at High SES (interaction -0.76, p=0.014); unadjusted, Black postsecondary exposure is lower at every SES level with the widest deficit at High SES (-6.4 pp). Hypothesis: the Black-non-Black difference in college attainment in these data does not depend on SES level — SES is a common, race-similar escalator — and any Black advantage is detectable only after adjustment for age and achievement, concentrated at lower-to-middle SES.
native_result.WorkflowB: Clean (grade 95 -> missing) -> outcomes BA>=16, any postsecondary >=13, >=17 -> composite family-of-origin SES index (z-scored parental education max of parents, log 1979 family income top-coded 75,001, occupation-at-14 mapped to ranked 1-digit 1970 census major groups; mean of >=2 of 3 available; tertiles) -> race x tertile rate tables with Wilson CIs -> Firth-penalized logit with race x tertile interaction (intercept unpenalized) -> age+ASVAB covariate check -> complete-case and PMM multiple-imputation (m=5, Rubin pooling) sensitivity -> winsorized later-SES (1985/89 income, 1985/90/96 wealth) sensitivity -> tertile gap tables. All rates are attainment-as-of-1979, right-censored.

sub_hypo.relations: BA completion is highest grade >=16. Black versus non-Black/non-Hispanic rates are 0.10% versus 0.12% at Low SES, 0.65% versus 0.25% at Mid SES, and 0.29% versus 0.63% at High SES. Race-by-SES-tertile interactions are non-significant in Firth logistic models (p=0.42/0.71) and PMM multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis (m=5, Rubin-pooled p=0.40/0.74). SES tertiles derive from the mean of at least two of three components: z-scored maximum parental education, log 1979 family income top-coded at 75,001, and occupation at age 14 mapped to ranked one-digit 1970 census major groups.
